prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: c021 (decay<=0.5, ignore_net_degree halved, adam scheme) is the best robust candidate; combining it with a *modest* per-net weight cap (the independently-successful c013/c016/c018 lineage showed TNS-heavy gains from capping max_net_weight) should spread weight to moderate nets while preventing a few early-critical nets from dominating — but do it inside timing.py so it applies regardless of the caller's max_net_weight, using a moderate cap factor rather than the aggressive 3.92.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.848 robust(mean-std)=+0.173 min_case=+0.155 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.270 dWNS=+11.9% dTNS=+37.0% overflow~144
  bp-ng45: score=+0.155 dWNS=+7.3% dTNS=+21.1% overflow~97
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.423 dWNS=+33.2% dTNS=+48.2% overflow~150
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: the modest in-timing.py cap preserved c021's robustness (all valid, min_case +0.155) while adding TNS-heavy gains. bp_fe-ng45 moved most (dWNS +33.2%, dTNS +48.2%), consistent with capping early-critical nets to spread weight to moderate nets; ariane133-ng45 and bp-ng45 also improved. Next step: sweep the cap factor between 1.0 and 3.92 (e.g. 1.5, 2.0, 2.5) to locate the optimum and confirm the moderate cap beats both no-cap and aggressive-cap baselines.
